patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in ecommerce, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Frame: Same category, different company size — Both sit in ecommerce, but documented company-size audiences diverge.. Choose Magento only if your buying job matches “Open-source Magento core (free) plus Adobe Commerce enterprise licenses (GMV quote) — deep” rather than Squarespace's shape. Choose Squarespace only if your buying job matches “Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanced $99/mo ” rather than Magento's shape. Workflow advantage: Magento leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b; Squarespace leans checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in ecommerce, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Magento is Open-source Magento core (free) plus Adobe Commerce enterprise licenses (GMV quote) — deep catalog/B2B with high hosting and agency TCO.; Squarespace is Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanced $99/mo annual (US 2026 tiles); platform transaction fees .
- Company-size focus: Magento (mid-market, enterprise) vs Squarespace (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Magento-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b, order-fulfillment vs Squarespace-leaning checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: Magento — Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0; Squarespace — Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume.

Limitations — Magento: Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0; Adobe Commerce pricing is opaque (GMV quote) — hard to compare without a partner worksheet; Squarespace: Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume; Catalog and B2B depth trail commerce-first platforms.

Poor-fit cases: Magento is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Operational and agency TCO is high versus hosted SaaS even when the Open Source license is $0 · Squarespace is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume · Avoid Magento if you actually need Squarespace's motion (Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanc)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
